# Open debts

**Generated by `just roadmap-debts`. Do not edit by hand — your edit will be overwritten,
and `just roadmap-debts --check` fails when this file and its sources disagree.**

Everything this engine has not finished, from four sources of decreasing strength. It is
a view over records that are already maintained for their own reasons rather than a fifth
place to keep up to date, because a hand-written list of unfinished work goes stale exactly
when it matters most — at the moment a milestone closes and somebody adds to it.

Closed milestones: M0, M1, M2, M3, M4, M5, M5.5, M6, M7, M8.a, M8.b, M8.c, M9, M10, M11.a, M11.b.

## 1. Declared gaps

A criterion that **runs, fails, and names the rung that must close it**. The strongest form,
because the ledger enforces both halves: an open gap keeps failing, and a gap that starts
*passing* fails the ledger with "THE GAP IS CLOSED, DELETE THE DECLARATION" — so it cannot
rot into something quietly fixed that nobody noticed.

The mechanism arrived at M8.c. Anything earlier is in section 4, unchecked.

**A row marked *retroactive* was written by a LATER rung over a gate that was already
green.** It is a declaration and a finding at once: the work is owed, and the rung whose
ledger carries the criterion closed without declaring it. A retroactive row therefore
appears in section 2 as well, because writing the declaration does not change what the
gate did.

## 2. Red criteria under a green gate

**A criterion of a milestone that has CLOSED, which the falsifiability record says was
FAILING — and which nobody declared as a gap.** The ledger's own arithmetic is that such a
criterion blocks: `selftest.test_declared_gaps` asserts in as many words that "an ordinary
failure beside a declared gap still fails the milestone". So every row below is a milestone
whose gate reads green over a check its own ledger fails, and it is not a margin — a rung
closes by a person flipping `state = "green"` in `gates.toml`, and **nothing in the tooling
compares that flip against the rung's own verdict.**

How it is read without an hour of running: `falsify.py` records `proven` for a criterion it
had to BREAK to make fail, and `red in the tree` / `red against a built tree` for one that
was already failing when it looked. For a rung that has closed, the second pair means the
check was red when the gate was flipped. A declared gap is excluded — that is section 1,
and the difference is the whole point: a gap is a failure somebody declared, dated and
pointed at a later rung, and what is here is a failure nobody declared at all.

**The ledger is the authority on what is red TODAY**; this is what the prover recorded, and
a row that has since gone green is a row whose recorded verdict `just roadmap-falsify check`
will report as stale.

**A row whose *Declared later by* cell is filled is a row a LATER rung declared as a gap.**
It stays here. The declaration says the work is owed and names the rung that owes it; it
does not reach back and make the closing flip honest, and the two statements are separate.
Such a row keeps its place whatever the *prover's verdict* column later reads: `falsify`
judges a declared gap the other way round — it owes a mutation that makes it GREEN — so a
gap with no `[criterion.falsifies]` is re-recorded as `no mutation` the next time anything
runs `just roadmap-falsify prove --record`. Nineteen of the twenty-one below are in exactly
that state, and reading this section off the verdict alone would have deleted them.

**THE GATES OF M11.a AND M11.b SHOULD NOT STAND AS THEY ARE READ TODAY.**
21 criteria below were red when those gates were flipped to
`state = "green"` in `tools/roadmap/gates.toml`, and by the ledger's own arithmetic —
"an ordinary failure beside a declared gap still fails the milestone" — a rung with a
red criterion nobody declared is not closed. The declarations written over them since
record the debt; they do not re-run the gate. Either those gates return to
`joins-on-close` until their ledgers pass, or `gates.toml` states in writing that they
were closed over named failures and which ones. **Only a Close phase may move a gate**,
so this document states the finding and moves nothing.

## 4. What each milestone said it did not close

Written prose in each archived change, and **nothing checks it**. This is the only record of
unfinished work before M8.c, because the declared-gap mechanism did not exist yet. Follow the
link for the detail rather than trusting the summary.

- **[2026-09-07-implement-m6-scale](../../openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-07-implement-m6-scale/tasks.md)** — Seven tasks above are deliberately unchecked. Each was reported by the agent that owned it or by the gate, with a reason, rather than being quietly ticked:
- **[2026-09-08-implement-m7-fidelity](../../openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-08-implement-m7-fidelity/tasks.md)** — Nineteen tasks above are unchecked. Each was reported by the agent that owned it or by the closing gate, with a reason, and the ledger's own notes carry the same list so a reader who never opens this file still finds them.
- **[2026-09-09-implement-m8a-authorable](../../openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-09-implement-m8a-authorable/tasks.md)** — Five tasks are unchecked. The milestone's own nineteen criteria are green and its artefact runs end to end; these are the edges the gate would not let pass as done.
- **[2026-09-11-implement-m8b-systems](../../openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-11-implement-m8b-systems/tasks.md)** — Thirteen tasks are unchecked. The ledger passes — 217 criteria, exit zero — and the slice plays.
- **[2026-09-11-implement-m8c-spectacle](../../openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-11-implement-m8c-spectacle/tasks.md)** — Thirteen tasks are unchecked. The ledger passes — 247 of 249 evaluated criteria — and the frame is captured rather than drawn, which is what this milestone was for.
- **[2026-09-11-implement-m9-integrity](../../openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-11-implement-m9-integrity/tasks.md)** — Sixteen tasks are unchecked. The ledger passes — 284 of 291 evaluated criteria, seven declared gaps — and the milestone's own artefact holds. These are the edges the gate would not let pass as done.
